allocations.requirement_text: The PCA pump should be able to operate within a temperature range9 of Tlo = 10C to Thi = 50C.10
The pump should be able to withstand and operate under atmospheric pressure 11 ranging from Pmin = 20”Hg to Pmax = 35”Hg.
The (external) pump should be able to operate at relative humidity 12 ranging from Hmin = 0% to Hmax = 100% (non-condensing).
The PCA pump shall withstand splashing 13 (but not immersion) with water or bodily fluids.

All filled prescriptions (liquid, narcotic pain-killer dispensed by the hospital pharmacy) must be labeled at least visibly with a. Patient name b. Drug code c. Name of drug d. Concentration e. Initial volume of drug f. Basal flow rate g. VTBI h. Minimum time between bolus i. Date prescription filled j. Prescribing physician’s name k. Pharmacist name
The PCA pump shall be cleaned and disinfected 154 after use.
The PCA pump must not leak current greater than 10 mA.
Component failure must not harm patient (beyond stopping function). 138

The PCA pump must be electromagnetically compatible 139 according to IEC 60601-1-2 (2001) Medical Electrical Equipment, Part 1: General Requirements for Safety, 2. Collateral Standard: Electromagnetic Compatibility - Requirements and Tests .
The PCA pump must withstand electrostatic discharge140.
The PCA pump must filter power interference 141 from mains.
The PCA pump shallissue alarms and warnings 42 that require clinician attention. (many EC)
The ICE Interface shall transmit current operating status and infusion rate to the ICE system.
The ICE interface shall transmit events, alarms, and warnings to the ICE system.
The ICE interface shall allow a clinician to set the duration of clinician-requested boluses through an ICE supervisor user interface.
The PCA pump shall switch to KVO infusion rate when commanded through its ICE interface.
The PCA pump shall resume prescribed infusion when commanded through its ICE interface.
Provisioning (or re-provisioning) shall not be possible through an ICE network.
The provisioning jack must be physically inaccessible, except to authorized technical personnel.162 Jacks for test equipment must be similarly inaccessible.
The provisioning jack must be physically inaccessible, except to authorized technical personnel.
The PCA pump shall detect power supply voltage out-of-range, issue a voltage out-of-range warn- ing 136, and switch to battery backup when out-of-range.
The PCA pump shall continue to infuse for 10 minutes during interruption of mains electricity supply using battery backup131, either continuously or spread over an hour.

Because with either working battery or power supply can operate the pump, if the battery failure alarm and either the voltage out-of-range or the power supply failure alarms, then the pump rate will be off, otherwise the pump rate will continue at its previous value.
The user interface must show that the PCA pump is working on battery backup, and an estimate of the number of minutes of battery-powered infusion remain.
The estimate of remaining battery energy must be accurate to within Xbtty = 25%.
If the estimated battery life remaining is less than ∆ lba = 3 minutes, the pump shall issue a low-battery warning 134.
The PCA pump shall detect battery failure and issue a battery failure alarm 135.
The PCA pump shall detect power supply voltage out-of-range, issue a voltage out-of-range warn- ing 136, and switch to battery backup when out-of-range.
The PCA pump shallissue alarms and warnings 42 that require clinician attention. (many EC)

If a visual indicator is necessary for the clinician to identify the equipment or part of the equipment that requires clinician response or awareness, at least one visual alarm signal 53 shall be provided that: 1. indicates the priority of the highest priority alarm condition; and 2. can be perceived correctly at a distance of 4 m from the PCA pump. (IEC 60601-1-8 2.3.1)
The alarm indicator appearance54 shall comply with color, flashing frequency, and duty cycle given in Table 5. (IEC 60601-1-8 2.3.1)
This signal shall be perceived correctly (be legible) at a distance of 1 m from the equipment or part of the equipment or from the clinician’s position.
Visual alarms shall display alarm symbols 56 from Table D.201 Graphical symbols for ALARM SYSTEMS of standard IEC 60601-1-8. (IEC 60601-1-8 2.3.1)
Alarms shall cause audible alarms signals 57 that meet the requirements of Tables 203 and 204 of standard IEC 60601-1-8 for alarm pulses, bursts, and harmonics. (IEC 60601-1-8 2.3.1)
The auditory volume 58 of audible alarms signals shall conform to Section 201.3.3.2 Volume of auditory ALARM SIGNALS and INFORMATION SIGNALS of standard IEC 60601-1-8. (IEC 60601-1-8 2.3.1)

The alarm melody 59 of audible alarms signals shall conform to Table AAA.1 of standard IEC 60601-1-8 for drug or fluid delivery. “C d g” shall be used for medium priority alarms; “C d g - C d” shall be used for high priority alarms; “e c” shall be used for warnings and low priority alarms. 60 (IEC 60601-1-8 2.3.1)
Each tone in the alarm melody shall be composed of a minimum of 4 harmonic components 61 in the range 300 Hz to 4000 Hz comprising an inverted 9th jazz chord. (IEC 60601-1-8 2.3.1)
The control panel shall allow clinician bolus request 68 and choice of duration. (UC3.1 §4.1.3)
The PCA pump shall resume prescribed infusion when the Start button is pressed. 84 (UC7 §4.1.7)
Pressing the stop button silences all alarms and terminates any alarm signal inactivation. 75 (UC6 §4.1.6)
The control panel shall allow clinician bolus request 68 and choice of duration. (UC3.1 §4.1.3)
Prescriptions that violate the soft limits of the drug in the drug library shall issue a visible and audible warning requiring a soft limit confirmation 69 by the clinician. (EC2 §4.2.2)
The Control Panel shall show alarm 71 condition as described in Section 6.4.2. 72 (IEC 60601-1-8 2.3.1)
The Control Panel shall audibly sound alarm 73 condition as described in Section 6.4.3. 74 (IEC 60601-1-8 2.3.1)
Pressing the stop button silences all alarms and terminates any alarm signal inactivation.
The Control Panel shall provide means toinactivate audible alarms indefinitely 76. (UC6 §4.1.6)
The Control Panel shall provide means to inactivate audible alarms temporarily 77 for a predefined period of time. (UC6.5 §4.1.6)
The Control Panel shall provide means to cancel alarm signal inactivation 78. (UC6.5 §4.1.6)

When auditory alarms are inactive the control panel shall display an inactive auditory alarm symbol79 from Table D.201 Graphical symbols for ALARM SYSTEMS of standard IEC 60601-1-8. (IEC 60601-1-8 2.3.1)
If the same alert-stop-start sequence 80 occurs 3 or more times in ten minutes, infusion will be stopped, and an audible alarm sounded. (EC23 §??)
sound of audible alarm 81, (UC1.2 §4.1.1 EC17 §4.2.17)
display of visual information 82, and (UC1.2 §4.1.1)
tactile response 83 (button press). (UC1.2 §4.1.1 EC17 §4.2.17)
The PCA pump shall resume prescribed infusion when the Start button is pressed.
The PCA pump shall display infusion rate 85 currently pumping. (UC1.15 §4.1.1)
A clinician must personally confirm the prescription is for the patient to be infused.

The basal flow rate 16, Fbasal, is prescribed by a physician, and entered into the PCA pump by scanning the prescription from the drug container label as it is loaded into the reservoir. (UC1.7 §4.1.1)

The pump shall maintain a minimum KVO flow rate 20 of FKV O = 1 ml/hr at all times during infusion, even during alarms, unless the alarm also stops flow, or the stop button is pressed. Table 4 defines which alarms also stop drug flow completely. (EC7.4 §4.2.7)

A patient-requested bolus 22 shall be delivered at its prescribed rate, Fbolus, in addition to the prescribed basal flow rate, Fbasal, but no more than the maximum flow rate for the pump, Fmax. (UC2.3 §4.1.2)
Any alarm stops basal rate 19 delivery either halting pump or switching to KVO rate as defined in Table 4. (many EC)
Any alarm stops patient-requested bolus 26 delivery either halting pump or switching to KVO rate as defined in Table 4. (many EC)

A clinician-requested bolus28 shall be delivered at the rate, Fccb, of V T BI divided by the duration chosen by the clinician, ∆ccb, in addition to the prescribed basal flow rate, Fbasal, but no more than the maximum flow rate for the pump, Fmax. (UC3.3 §4.1.3) Fccb = min(V T BI/∆ccb + Fbasal, Fmax)

A patient-requested bolus takes precedence29 over a clinician-requested bolus. The clinician-requested bolus shall be suspended while the patient-requested bolus dose is administered, and resumed afterward. (UC3.3 §4.1.3)
Any alarm halts clinician-requested bolus 30 delivery either halting pump or switching to KVO rate as defined in Table 4. (many EC)

Patient-requested bolus shall not be delivered if infusing prescribed V T BI will exceed hard limits retrieved from the drug library for the volume of drug infused over a period of time. Pump rate shall be reduced to KVO and a max dose warning 25 be issued. (EC13 §4.2.13)
The mechanical pump shall halt pumping 39 when commanded, or caused in response to an alarm condition.(many EC)
Upon the clinician’s pressing of the start button, start infusion 64 prescribed. (UC1.14 §4.1.1 UC7.1 §4.1.7)
Upon the clinician’s pressing of the stop button, stop infusion 67. (UC1.16 §4.1.1)
Before infusion, the door must be closed and locked.
Prescribed V T BI and rate shall not exceed the maximum VTBI 24 limit set by the drug library from the hospital pharmacy for the drug loaded in the PCA pump. (EC3 §4.2.3)
The maximum clinician-chosen duration 31 for a clinician-requested bolus shall be ∆ ccb max = 6 hours.
The minimum clinician-chosen duration 32 for a clinician-requested bolus shall be the prescribed minimum number of minutes between consecutive patient-requested bolus deliveries, ∆ prb.
The PCA pump shall use a physician’s prescription as device parameters41. (UC1 §4.1.1 UC2 §4.1.2 UC3 §4.1.3)
Prescriptions that violate a hard limit 70 of the drug in the drug library shall be rejected with visible and audible indication when confirmation is attempted by the clinician. (EC3 §4.2.3)
Prescriptions that violate the soft limits of the drug in the drug library shall issue a visible and audible warning requiring a soft limit confirmation 69 by the clinician. (EC2 §4.2.2)
The patient’s prescription shall be retained for at least.∆ data = 96 hours after the PCA pump is turned-off and unplugged.
A clinician must personally confirm the prescription is for the patient to be infused.
The ICE Interface shall transmit current operating status and infusion rate to the ICE system.
The ICE interface shall transmit events, alarms, and warnings to the ICE system.
The ICE interface shall allow a clinician to set the duration of clinician-requested boluses through an ICE supervisor user interface.
The PCA pump shall switch to KVO infusion rate when commanded through its ICE interface.
The PCA pump shall resume prescribed infusion when commanded through its ICE interface.
When the PCA pump is not connected to an ICE network, or the ICE network connection fails, the PCA pump shall operate as a singular, stand-alone device.
The ICE interface may inactivate alarms.
Clinicians authorization to operate the PCA pump must be authenticated.
Patient’s identity and admittance to the hospital must be authenticated.
Drug container must have a valid prescription for the particular patient to be infused by the PCA pump.
Drug library information shall be authenticated before it is accepted.

Patient-requested bolus shall not be delivered if infusing prescribed V T BI will exceed hard limits retrieved from the drug library for the volume of drug infused over a period of time. Pump rate shall be reduced to KVO and a max dose warning 25 be issued. (EC13 §4.2.13)
Patient-requested bolus shall not be delivered more often than a prescribed minimum time between patient-requested bolus23, ∆prb. (UC2.2 §4.1.2)
The drug loaded into the reservoir must also be found in the PCA pump’s drug in library.
The drug code of the prescription must match the drug code of a drug library entry.
The drug code of the prescription must match the drug code of a drug library entry.
Before commencing infusion, the values of V T BI and Fbasal are checked against the drug library entry of the drug to be infused.
Pump remains stopped.
The PCA pump shall maintain an electronic event log 86 to record each action taken by the pump and each event sensed of its environment. (no UC or EC specific to logging)
Each log entry shall have a time stamp 88 with its time of occurrence.
Information in event and Fault Logs shall be retained for at least ∆ log = 1000 hours after the PCA pump is turned-off and unplugged.
The event log shall record 30 days of typical events before overwriting oldest event records first.

A patient-requested bolus 22 shall be delivered at its prescribed rate, Fbolus, in addition to the prescribed basal flow rate, Fbasal, but no more than the maximum flow rate for the pump, Fmax. (UC2.3 §4.1.2)

The basal flow rate 16, Fbasal, is prescribed by a physician, and entered into the PCA pump by scanning the prescription from the drug container label as it is loaded into the reservoir. (UC1.7 §4.1.1)
The PCA pump shall use a physician’s prescription as device parameters41. (UC1 §4.1.1 UC2 §4.1.2 UC3 §4.1.3)
Prior to, or coincident with, loading the drug reservoir must also enter prescription on the drug container’s label using the scanner.
The scanner shall read and authenticate information from the patient’s wristband116.
The scanner shall read and authenticate information from the clinician’s badge117.
The scanner shall read and authenticate information from the drug’s package label 118.
Clinicians authorization to operate the PCA pump must be authenticated.
Patient’s identity and admittance to the hospital must be authenticated.
Drug container must have a valid prescription for the particular patient to be infused by the PCA pump.
Drug library information shall be authenticated before it is accepted.
Patient information must be restricted to those providing care for the patient, and the patient.
Provisioning (or re-provisioning) shall not be possible through an ICE network.
Provisioning shall be a single, unitary block-transfer.
All materials that contact fluid shall be biocompatible153.
The pump shall be able to deliver basal infusion at flows throughout the basal infusion flow range 17 of Fbasal min = 1 to Fbasal max = 10 ml/hr. (UC1 §4.1.1)
The pump shall deliver basal infusion at the prescribed basal rate within a basal infusion flow tolerance18 of Fbasal tol = 0.5 ml/hr of the prescribed basal rate. (UC1.12 §4.1.1)
The mechanical pump shall pump drug 38 at prescribed flow rates for basal, bolus, and KVO infusion when commanded. (UC1 §4.1.1 UC2 §4.1.2 UC3 §4.1.3)
The mechanical pump shall halt pumping 39 when commanded, or caused in response to an alarm condition.(many EC)
If the pump gets overheated to more than Tpoh = 55 C, the pump shall issue an pump overheated alarm 49 (EC4.2.9).
When the stop button is pressed, the current pump stroke shall be completed prior to stopping the pump.
During normal use and/or single fault condition of the equipment, continuous reverse delivery 121 shall not be possible.
An upstream occlusion alarm124 shall be triggered when the pump senses an upstream (drug reservoir side) occlusion exceeding Puo = 1 psi.
The mechanical pump shall not allow reverse flow 40 from the patient into the pump. (FDA ??)
The PCA pump shall measure drug flow 34 within a tolerance of Fmd f tol = 0 .1 ml/hr. (many EC)
The PCA pump shall detect upstream occlusion36. (EC11 §4.2.11)
The PCA pump shall measure drug flow 34 within a tolerance of Fmd f tol = 0 .1 ml/hr. (many EC)
The PCA pump shall detect downstream occlusion35. (EC10 §4.2.10)
The PCA pump shall detect air-in-line embolism 37 (bubble). (EC12 §4.2.12)
The drug reservoir holds liquid pain-killer supplied by the hospital pharmacy and loaded into the PCA pump by the clinician.
The drug reservoir shall measure its contents.
The measured drug volume shall be within Vrt = 1 ml of the actual drug volume.
If the drug volume in the reservoir measures less than Vlra = 1 ml, and an infusion is in progress, a low-reservoir warning shall be issued.
If the drug volume in the reservoir measures less than Vers =0.5 ml, and an infusion is in progress, an empty-reservoir alarm shall be issued stopping the pump.

Because the drugs used for analgesia are often narcotic, requiring Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) tracking if used in the United States, the drug reservoir and means to change prescriptions during infusion must be inhibited with a locked, tamper-resistant door149.

Hospital procedures must endow the attending clinician access to the door key 151, yet prevent other persons’ access. Key-handling processes are beyond the scope of these requirements, but much depends on the attending clinician: it’s the right drug, in the right patient, with the right prescription from a physician authorized to prescribe narcotics for those suffering great pain.
The PCA pump case 152 must be at least difficult to breech as its tamper-resistant door. Breaking the case shall not be easier to access the drug reservoir than breeching the door.
An open door alarm 130 shall be triggered when the reservoir door is opened while the pump is not stopped.
The PCA pump shall implement a safety architecture119 that separates normal operation from fault detection and response.
Hardware faults that prevent operation of the Control Panel shall illuminate a hardware fault indicator148 (light-emitting diode). (EC22f §4.2.22)
The PCA pump shallissue alarms and warnings 42 that require clinician attention. (many EC)

If delivered basal flow rate exceeds the prescribed basal rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 5 minutes, or immediately if the pump goes into free flow, the pump shall issue an basal over-infusion alarm 43 (EC7 §4.2.7).

If delivered basal flow rate is less than the prescribed basal rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 5 minutes, or immediately if the flow stops, the pump shall issue an basal under-infusion warning 44 (EC4.2.8).

If delivered patient-requested bolus flow rate exceeds the prescribed patient-requested bolus rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 1 minutes, or immediately if the pump goes into free flow, the pump shall issue a bolus over-infusion alarm 45 (EC4.2.7).

If delivered patient-requested bolus flow rate is less than the prescribed bolus rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 1 minutes, or immediately if the flow stops, the pump shall issue a bolus under-infusion warning 46 (EC4.2.8).

If delivered clinician-requested bolus flow rate exceeds the calculated square bolus rate by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 5 minutes, or immediately if the pump goes into free flow, the pump shall issue a square bolus over-infusion alarm 47 (EC4.2.7).

If delivered clinician-requested bolus flow rate is less than the calculated square bolus rate by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 5 minutes, or immediately if the flow stops, the pump shall issue a square bolus under-infusion warning 48 (EC4.2.8).
If the pump gets overheated to more than Tpoh = 55 C, the pump shall issue an pump overheated alarm 49 (EC4.2.9).

Alarm’s and warning’s priority 50 shall be determined in accordance with standard IEC 60601-1-8 Medical electrical equipment - Part 1-8: General requirements for safety - Collateral standard: Alarm systems - General requirements, tests and guidance for alarm systems in medical electrical equipment and medical electrical systems . Table 201 - Alarm Condition Priorities is reproduced as Table 3 for convenience. (IEC 60601-1-8 2.3.1)

Priority for alarms and warnings is shown in Table 4; warnings are low-priority alarms. The last column show the alarm pump rate 51 to be used while the alarm is in effect. For “special” flow rates for power malfunctions see Section 7.3.
An air-in-line alarm 122 shall be triggered by the pump if detectable air bubbles are infused into the patient.123
An upstream occlusion alarm124 shall be triggered when the pump senses an upstream (drug reservoir side) occlusion exceeding Puo = 1 psi.
A downstream occlusion alarm125 shall be triggered if the pump senses a downstream (patient side) occlusion exceeding Pdo = 10 psi.
An upstream occlusion alarm124 shall be triggered when the pump senses an upstream (drug reservoir side) occlusion exceeding Puo = 1 psi.
When an empty-reservoir alarm 128 occurs, the current pump stroke shall be completed prior to stopping the pump. 129

If delivered basal flow rate exceeds the prescribed basal rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 5 minutes, or immediately if the pump goes into free flow, the pump shall issue an basal over-infusion alarm 43 (EC7 §4.2.7).

If delivered basal flow rate is less than the prescribed basal rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 5 minutes, or immediately if the flow stops, the pump shall issue an basal under-infusion warning 44 (EC4.2.8).

If delivered patient-requested bolus flow rate exceeds the prescribed patient-requested bolus rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 1 minutes, or immediately if the pump goes into free flow, the pump shall issue a bolus over-infusion alarm 45 (EC4.2.7).

If delivered patient-requested bolus flow rate is less than the prescribed bolus rate setting by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 1 minutes, or immediately if the flow stops, the pump shall issue a bolus under-infusion warning 46 (EC4.2.8).

If delivered clinician-requested bolus flow rate exceeds the calculated square bolus rate by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 5 minutes, or immediately if the pump goes into free flow, the pump shall issue a square bolus over-infusion alarm 47 (EC4.2.7).

If delivered clinician-requested bolus flow rate is less than the calculated square bolus rate by more than its allowed tolerance over a period of more than 5 minutes, or immediately if the flow stops, the pump shall issue a square bolus under-infusion warning 48 (EC4.2.8).

The PCA pump shall perform a power-on self-test 142 (POST) to assure system integrity after being turned on, yet before any infusion begins. Failure of POST shall raise a POST alarm , stop pump, record it in the Fault Log, and display the reason for failure on the user interface. (EC4 §4.2.4)

The PCA pump shall perform periodic self-tests 143 to assure system integrity during long periods of use. Failure of a self-test shall raise a self-test alarm , stop pump, record it in the Fault Log, and display the reason for failure on the user interface. (EC22c §4.2.22)
The PCA pump shall have continuous fault-detection144 and masking. Hardware monitors of thread heartbeat, memory error correction codes are examples. (EC22d §4.2.22)
Occurrence of unavoidable single-event upsets 145 caused by cosmic-ray-induced high- and thermal-energy neutrons must be either masked, or detected to fail-stop. (EC22d §4.2.22)
If the drug loaded into the drug reservoir is not present in the drug library, that the drug is unknown is indicated by the user interface, and recorded in the Fault Log.
Each log entry shall have a time stamp 88 with its time of occurrence.
Information in event and Fault Logs shall be retained for at least ∆ log = 1000 hours after the PCA pump is turned-off and unplugged.
Successfully masked faults 146 shall be recorded in the Fault Log, but not raise an alarm. (EC22e §4.2.22)
All unmasked hardware detected faults147 shall raise a fault alarm, stop pump, record it in the Fault Log, and display the reason for fault on the user interface. (EC22 §4.2.22)
The fault log shall record at least 1000 faults before overwriting oldest fault records first.
A real-time clock93 must produce timestamps accurate to 10 ms.
